findings.detail: audited drawing does not depict this option — This is the Curved 9.0 cm drawing. It is annotated '125.00' degrees - the exact same value as curved-in-9cm.jpg - and a red/blue ink overlay of the two shows them registering line-for-line (same leaf shape, same tip position, same stand front, same throat button); only resampling fringe separates them. A French collar per the catalog is 'extremely wide-spread, with points that angle dramatically toward the shoulder seams', and the house does have that drawing: french-in-8cm.jpg is annotated '145.00' degrees with a visibly much wider spread. At 125 degrees this is a curved collar, and the customer would see the identical picture on both the French 7.5 cm and Curved 9.0 cm options.

audited drawing does not depict this option — The catalog defines this as 'A 5.0 cm upright band collar with NO fold-over leaf, circling the neck cleanly in the Mandarin or Nehru manner.' The drawing shows the opposite: a wide-spread TURNDOWN collar with two fold-over leaves crossing at the front, a rounded stand front with a button, annotated '145.00' degrees. It is also effectively the same drawing as french-in-8cm.jpg (0.052) and regular-collar-21.jpg (0.053), both '145.00'. The folder does contain genuine band-collar drawings (rolled-stand-collar.jpg, the one-piece-collar-in-*cm files) and they look nothing like this. Note this file is byte-identical to /images/techpacks/shirt/lapel/stand-collar-5cm.jpg (md5 256fa79278d5b76b214066fce69f53d2).

audited drawing does not depict this option — Shows a low rounded BAND/stand collar with no fold-over leaf and no collar points at all, closed at the centre front with a single button on the band. There is no tab. The house style does draw a real tab - regular-collar-in-85cm-with-tab.jpg in the same folder shows the collar leaves open with a horizontal fabric tab strip bridging them, bar-tacked, annotated '60.00' degrees. This drawing is instead nearly the same as rolled-stand-collar.jpg (shape distance 0.059) and one-piece-collar-in-75cm-with-tab.jpg (0.040). Neither the turndown one-piece leaf nor the tab is depicted.

audited drawing does not depict this option — An upright mandarin/band collar: front edges butt together at a plain vertical seam, no fold-over leaf, no collar points, no button on the band (only a small button-and-loop further down the placket), and no tab anywhere. Line art is also washed out and low-contrast (smallest file in the folder at 4192 bytes). Compare regular-collar-in-85cm-with-tab.jpg, which shows an actual throat tab. Neither 'One-Piece' turndown construction nor 'with Tab' is depicted.

audited drawing does not depict this option — Same failure as its 8.0 and 8.5 cm siblings: an upright band/stand collar with a narrow vertical underlap strip at the centre front, no fold-over leaf, no collar points, and no throat tab. Clusters with one-piece-collar-in-85cm-with-tab.jpg (0.065) and squared-stand-collar.jpg (0.095) rather than with any tab-collar drawing. The 'with Tab' feature named in the label is absent.

audited drawing does not depict this option — Not a point collar at all. It is the shared 'collar worn open' template - collar unbuttoned, leaves splayed flat, deep V, loop-and-button at the left front, no dimension annotation - and it registers almost exactly on cuban-collar.jpg (shape distance 0.031), standard-collar-with-75cm-collar-stand.jpg (0.025) and point-in-85cm-with-button.jpg (0.029). The house's actual 5.8 cm point collars in the same folder (fashion-point-in-58cm.jpg and point-in-58cm-with-button.jpg) are drawn CLOSED with short points and a blue '60.00' degree annotation. This drawing shows neither the 5.8 cm short point nor any dimension.

audited drawing does not depict this option — Drawing shows a DOUBLE (folded) cuff with 4 buttonholes and MITRED/ANGLED corners — not a rounded barrel cuff, and no buttons at all. The flat view is a double-height rectangle with a mid fold line, V-notched (chamfered) corners at both ends, and 4 identical pale-blue buttonhole dashes; the elevation view shows a straight 45-degree cut corner, not a curve. Its mark layout is pixel-for-pixel the same configuration as its sibling french-cuff-with-4-buttonholes.jpg (same 187x244-class canvas, same non-red house style), differing only in corner treatment. Every genuine 'round cuff' sibling in this catalog (round-cuff-with-1-button-and-1-buttonhole.jpg, round-cuff-with-2-buttons-and-2-buttonholes.jpg, round-french-cuff-with-4-buttonholes.jpg) is a 192x192 drawing with a RED-highlighted flat cuff carrying distinct plus-shaped BUTTON glyphs and slot-shaped BUTTONHOLE glyphs — this file has neither red highlight nor any button glyph. Catalog text for cuff-round-2btn-1bh reads 'a barrel cuff with rounded outer corners secured by two buttons', while the sibling option cuff-hex-french-4bh is described as 'a double cuff whose folded edge is cut with an angled, mitered corner' — which is exactly what this image depicts. Wrong variant: this is a hexagon/cut-corner French cuff, not a round 2-button barrel cuff.
